items.title: Holocene avulsion history of the Euphrates and Tigris rivers in the Mesopotamian floodplain
items.note: Maps palaeochannels from satellite imagery, coring and dating to reconstruct shifting river courses, the framework any Tigris-side placement of Agade depends on.

items.title: The Age of Agade: Inventing Empire in Ancient Mesopotamia
items.note: Standard synthesis of the Sargonic period that summarizes the textual case for a location on the Tigris and leaves the site unidentified.

items.title: New Insights on the Role of Environmental Dynamics Shaping Southern Mesopotamia: From the Pre-Ubaid to the Early Islamic Period
items.who: M. R. Altaweel, A. Marsh, J. Jotheri et al.
items.note: Reviews geoarchaeological evidence for channel migration, marine incursion and sedimentation across the alluvium, including the uncertain third-millennium courses of the Tigris.

items.title: Fluch über Akkade
items.note: New annotated German translation of the Curse of Agade, the main literary source on the city's rise, fall and cultic topography.

items.title: The Kingdom of Akkad in Contact with the World
items.venue: The Oxford History of the Ancient Near East, vol. 1
items.note: Handbook account of the Sargonic state that treats the capital as still unlocated and stresses how little of its administration survives.

items.title: GIS and Historical Geographical Analyses of the Reconstructed Ancient Course of the Tigris in the Northern Part of Southern Mesopotamia
items.note: Tests earlier claims of an eastern ancient Tigris against SRTM and ALOS elevation models, CORONA imagery and textual topography to reconstruct the river's course.

items.title: Searching for the location of the ancient city of Akkade in relation to the ancient course of the Tigris using historical and GIS analyses
items.note: Combines the reconstructed Tigris course with textual itineraries to narrow a candidate search zone for Akkade, the first explicitly GIS-based proposal.

items.title: The Location of the Ancient City of Akkade: Review of Past Theories and Identification of Issues for Formulating a Specific Methodology for Searching Akkade
items.note: Reviews the main location theories since the nineteenth century and sets out the problems a field search would need to resolve.

items.title: Capital of the World's First Empire
items.note: Popular survey of the search; reports N. Ziegler's preference for the Adhaim-Tigris confluence based on an Old Babylonian convoy itinerary from Eshnunna to Mari.
